questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Do not brake until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: You are already in an intersection when a green light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through and clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger vehicles. At 55 mph, a passenger vehicle can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs about 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be ticketed.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If fog is so thick you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds in a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down accordingly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance is present.

questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction and maintenance areas. They help guide drivers and pedestrians safely through work zones. Traffic fines may be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
Slow down gradually and not brake.
Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow by itself. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather?

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: In rain, lower your speed to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes your tires to ride on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield to the pedestrian.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind or partially blind. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. They alert drivers that bicycles, animals, or pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and be careful.
Quickly move to the next lane.

questions.explanation: Animals can suddenly move into the road without warning. Slow down and proceed carefully. There may also be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: How can you see what is behind your vehicle?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out the back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: If you are 16 or 17 and convicted of speeding more than 20 mph over the limit, your license will be suspended for how long?

options.text: 30 days.
45 days.
60 days.

questions.explanation: For a first offense, drivers aged 16 or 17 will lose their license for 60 days. They must also pay a restoration fee and court fines. Penalties are stricter for repeat offenses.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for them to merge, if you can.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them to merge, if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, allow merging traffic to enter your lane.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Stop and take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Pull over at the next rest area to nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. They do not replace sleep and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: Do not speed up when being passed. Keep your speed constant and let the other vehicle pass safely.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in your mirrors. You must turn and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: What happens when drivers slow down to look at accidents or unusual events?

options.text: It causes traffic jams.
It prevents rear-end collisions.
It improves traffic flow.

questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or other events. This is called "rubbernecking" and it creates traffic congestion.

questions.question: When driving near a distracted driver, how far back should you stay?

options.text: One to two seconds.
Two to three seconds.
Three to four seconds.

questions.explanation: Stay at least three to four seconds behind a distracted driver. Be extra careful when passing them. They may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect driving on highways?

options.text: Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust onto the road. It can also physically move your vehicle.

questions.question: When is it most dangerous to turn or stop in rainy weather?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with the rain, making the road very slippery.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware. Do not stare only at the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.explanation: Weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex, how much food is in your stomach, and how many drinks you have had. Only time removes alcohol from your system.
